The only thing really stopping me to switch to linux is my gaming-hobby (I have a linux home server running, so I have a little knowledge about linux). I know the linux-games list is growing and there are things available like WINE or PlayOnLinux, but these things seems like on game-patch away to not work properly again (at least for a time).

So I asked my good friend google "windows gaming through VM", I think you get the idea of it. I found out that gaming on windows through an VM is kinda bad, because VM don't support 3d hardware acceleration or in other words "Windows can't acces the full power of the graphic card". In the Ubunto-Forum I found a post that spiked my attention:

"[...] A hypervisor would probably solve your problem, as you can switch quickly between Windows and Ubuntu without having to reboot. You need suitable hardware, however: a 64-bit machine with virtualisation support (you may have to enable it in your BIOS), and sufficient RAM; I suspect 4Gb would suffice. The default hypervisor for Ubuntu is KVM, but there are others such as Xen. [...]"

It took a few seconds more to find a tutorial HOW-TO make dual-boot obsolete using XEN VGA passthrough, and don't get exited to quickly - it hase some hardware requirements to run properly.

So my questions are: Has anybody treid this? (does it work? and when yes, how good?); or is there another alternative to this?
Yes, but you can use internal graphics like an integrated GPU on your CPU and then a dedicated graphics card. So run Linux on the integrated GPU and the VM passthrough takes the dedicated GPU.
